definition.def: If you stress a point in a discussion, you put extra emphasis on it because you think it is important.
examples: The spokesman stressed that the measures did not amount to an overall ban. [VERB that]
They stress the need for improved employment opportunities. [VERB noun]
'We're not saying we're outside and above all this,' he stresses. [VERB with quote]

definition.def: If you feel under stress, you feel worried and tense because of difficulties in your life.
examples: Katy could think clearly when not under stress.
Of course, the British will suffer such daily stresses patiently.

definition.def: Stresses are strong physical pressures applied to an object.
examples: Earthquakes happen when stresses in rock are suddenly released as the rocks fracture.

definition.def: If you stress a word or part of a word when you say it, you put emphasis on it so that it sounds slightly louder.
examples: 'Sit down,' she replied, stressing each word. [VERB noun]
